summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as teams scale LLM applications and need visibility into prompts, traces, costs, quality, and hallucinations. The market grew to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR, reflecting how critical monitoring is for controlling costs, ensuring reliability, and meeting compliance requirements. Choosing the right tool depends on your framework, deployment needs, and whether cost tracking or deep evaluation is the priority.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Prompts, traces, agent workflows, token usage, latency, and evaluation metrics—with zero-config tracing for LangChain/LangGraph apps.
features: Deep LangChain/LangGraph integration with automatic tracing
Latency and token/cost tracking per trace
tools.pricing: Seat-based plus usage; free tier available. Per-trace overage charges can add up to roughly 5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy, high-volume workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain or LangGraph who want zero-config framework tracing and integrated evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API request/response logs, token usage, cost per user/department, latency, and caching—via a lightweight proxy.
features: One-line proxy integration (change only the base URL)
Granular cost tracking by user, department, or model
tools.pricing: Usage/request-based with a generous free tier; cost governance can be set up in under five minutes.
tools.best_for: Teams focused primarily on fast, low-overhead cost monitoring and visibility into OpenAI/LLM spend.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: Model experiments, training runs, LLM traces (via W&B Weave), prompts, evaluations, and production performance.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Integration across ML and LLM workflows
tools.pricing: Seat/usage-based with a free tier for individuals; enterprise plans for teams.
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams wanting a unified platform spanning model training experiments and LLM observability.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML performance, traces, embeddings, drift, data quality, and evaluation metrics.
features: Open-source Arize Phoenix for tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize offers usage-based cloud and enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Teams needing robust production monitoring, drift detection, and RAG/embedding evaluation at scale.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: Traces, prompts, token usage, costs, latency, and evaluation scores across multiple frameworks.
features: Open-source and fully self-hostable for data residency/compliance
Multi-framework support (not tied to one SDK)
Cost and token tracking per trace
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosting is free (compute + storage only); managed cloud offers free and usage-based paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams needing self-hosting, multi-framework support, or compliance-driven data control as a cost-effective alternative.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, latency, and costs using open standards, exportable to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend.
features: Vendor-neutral—export to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.
Automatic instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs come only from the backend/observability platform you export to.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation that plugs into existing observability stacks.

cost_tips: Use response caching (e.g., via Helicone or a proxy layer) to avoid paying for repeated or near-identical requests.
Route requests intelligently: use smaller, cheaper models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Set per-user, per-department, and per-model budgets with alerts so trace/token overages don't silently inflate spend—note LangSmith per-trace overages can reach 5–10% of LLM API spend at high volume.
Optimize prompts and context: trim unnecessary tokens, truncate long histories, and use retrieval to send only relevant context, reducing input token costs.
Consider self-hosting open-source tools like Langfuse or Arize Phoenix to eliminate per-trace SaaS fees for high-volume workloads.
